items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: And he and I were in Booker T. Washington's band, and we made up, all of Booker T. Washington's band made up a swing band.

ctx.x: What's the band then, you'd have what, two, two tenets? What do you mean, a saxophone? It was a big band.

It was a big band. It was a big band. Well, there was four or five saxophones. But four saxophones, I'd say, three trumpets and a trombone. Some would have two trumpets, it was a small band, but at that time, like Herbert Liris' band, I used, my uncle August was playing with them and he'd bring me around just to be around the musicians and listen at the band. Even before I was playing music, when I was thirteen, thirteen years old. I remember because they had four saxophones and they had three trumpets and two…

items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: he and I were in Booker T. Washington's band... Louis Sergin is his name... But he and I played alto sax.

ctx.x: Yeah. And he and I were in Booker T. Washington's band, and we made up, all of Booker T. Washington's band made up a swing band. We got Hogan, he was dead, a drummer. He didn't have a set of drums. He had to borrow a bass drum from somebody, and he had a snare drum, stands. And I had alto sax and another guy named Fuzzy, he was playing alto, he was in the band also. Who's that? Melvin Lastic. Louis Sergin is his name, he's not in New Orleans now, he went to California. But he and I played alto sax. Joe Jones was…
And you could play by ear though?
